items.title: The Vikings Didn't Just Steal Gold — They Stole People 😳
items.description:
Did you know that Vikings captured people and sold them into slavery?

The Vikings didn't just steal treasure — they captured and traded human beings.

Captives taken during raids in the British Isles and Eastern Europe could be sold at trading centres including Hedeby and Bolghar, or forced to work as thralls. Viking-era slavery is documented in written sources and archaeology.

Cinematic AI-generated historical reconstruction; not archival footage.

Source: National Museum of Denmark — Slaves and thralls: https://en.natmus.dk/historical-knowledge/denmark/prehistoric-period-until-1050-ad/the-viking-age/power-and-aristocracy/slaves-and-thralls/

items.title: The Treasure Hidden for 1,100 Years 💰 | Galloway Hoard
items.description:
Somebody buried a treasure in Scotland around AD 900. In 2014, a metal detectorist discovered what became known as the Galloway Hoard: over 100 fascinating Viking-age objects, including silver, gold, and even preserved textiles. Who buried it — and why — remains a mystery.

AI-generated historical reconstruction; the person who hid the hoard is unknown, so their depiction is illustrative, not verified history.

Sources: National Museums Scotland: https://www.nms.ac.uk/discover-catalogue/galloway-hoard and https://www.nms.ac.uk/discover-catalogue/what-is-the-galloway-hoard

items.title: People Died Searching for a Treasure Nobody Found 😳 | Oak Island
items.description:
For more than 200 years, people have searched Oak Island, Nova Scotia, for a legendary buried treasure. Water-filled shafts and tragic accidents became part of the mystery. But no hidden flood-trap network or legendary hoard has been conclusively proven.

AI-generated cinematic reconstruction. The 1795 origin story is a later legend, not a verified first-hand account.

items.title: Did the Knights Templar Hide Their Treasure? 😱 | 1307
items.description:
On 13 October 1307, Philip IV ordered the arrest of the Knights Templar in France. Their properties were seized, and centuries of legends grew around a supposed hidden treasure. Was any fortune secretly moved before the arrests? There is no reliable evidence for the popular treasure-escape story.

AI-generated cinematic historical reconstruction. The supposed secret transport of chests is shown as an unverified legend, not a historical event.

Background: National Geographic interviews with medieval historians about the Knights Templar, 1307 arrests, and treasure myths.
Music: Epical Drums 04 by Grigoriy Nuzhny, Mixkit Stock Music Free License.

items.title: Did a Pastry Shop Help Start a War? 😳 | 1838
items.description:
In 1838, France blockaded Veracruz after Mexico rejected a 600,000-peso compensation demand involving several French claims—including damage to a pastry shop. The bakery gave the conflict its unforgettable nickname, but cake was never the whole cause.
